definitions.gloss: new word; neologism; newly coined term
definitions.explanation: A word or expression that has been newly created or recently entered the language. Includes loanwords, slang, and technical terms that reflect changes in society and culture.

examples.japanese: ⟦{毎年|まいとし}→毎年：00731_maitoshi⟧{新語|しんご}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{生|う}まれる→生まれる：00905_umareru⟧。
examples.english: New words are born every year.

examples.japanese: {新語|しんご}・⟦{流行語|りゅうこうご}→流行語：13307_ryuukougo⟧⟦{大賞|たいしょう}→大賞：12191_taishou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{発表|はっぴょう}→発表：03562_happyou⟧⟦された→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: The New Words and Buzzwords of the Year Award was announced.

examples.japanese: ⟦インターネット→インターネット：04723_intaanetto⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{普及|ふきゅう}→普及：07592_fukyuu⟧⟦とともに→とともに：30485_totomoni⟧、{多|おお}く⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{新語|しんご}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{日本語|にほんご}→日本語：00614_nihongo⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{入|はい}って→入る：00494_hairu⟧きた。
examples.english: Along with the spread of the internet, many new words have entered Japanese.

notes:
Composed of {新|しん} (new) and ⟦{語|ご}→〜語：09841_go⟧ (word, language). Refers to words that have recently appeared in the language.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {新語|しんご}・⟦{流行語|りゅうこうご}→流行語：13307_ryuukougo⟧⟦{大賞|たいしょう}→大賞：12191_taishou⟧: New Words and Buzzwords of the Year Award
- {新語|しんご}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{生|う}まれる→生まれる：00905_umareru⟧: new words are coined
- {新語|しんご}⟦{辞典|じてん}→辞典：01640_jiten⟧: dictionary of new words
- {新語|しんご}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}る→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧: to coin a new word

CULTURAL NOTE:
The annual {新語|しんご}・⟦{流行語|りゅうこうご}→流行語：13307_ryuukougo⟧⟦{大賞|たいしょう}→大賞：12191_taishou⟧ (New Words and Buzzwords of the Year Award) is a popular year-end event in Japan, announced each December. It reflects social trends and cultural phenomena of that year.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{流行語|りゅうこうご}→流行語：13307_ryuukougo⟧: buzzword — a word that becomes temporarily popular
- {新語|しんご}: neologism — a newly created or adopted word
- ⟦{造語|ぞうご}→造語：25313_zougo⟧: coined word — emphasizes that the word was deliberately invented
- ⟦{廃語|はいご}→廃語：26501_haigo⟧: obsolete word — the opposite, a word that has fallen out of use
